terms.comment: Not in Lewis & Short, and no ancient name for lavender is certain. Morgan–Owens gives lavendula from a tenth-century source (after the OED) and from thirteenth- and seventeenth-century sources (after Latham), and lavandula from a sixteenth-century source (after Latham) and from Linnaeus, who made it the name of the genus: so the word is medieval, and the spelling with a is the later and the botanists’. Left unmarked, as Morgan–Owens leaves it and as Traupman leaves it in lavandulāceus, lavender-coloured. Pliny’s stoechas, a scented herb of the Stoechades islands (NH 27.131), lives on in the botanists’ Lavandula stoechas; it is not in Lewis & Short, and is not entered here.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. lavender.
